notes: Personal wellness tool, not medical advice. ~30 questions, about 5 minutes. Validated items: SNAQ (4, verbatim), AEBQ Satiety Responsiveness (4) and Hunger (5) (verbatim, CC BY). MNA-SF items A and B paraphrased (copyrighted) and unscored safety flags only. Everything else is a practical intake question marked evidence 'limited'. Left out for lack of fit or evidence: full CNAQ (its item about taste 'compared to when I was 50' does not fit a 45-year-old; SNAQ is its validated short form from the same paper); AEBQ Emotional Under-eating and Slowness in Eating (valid, but cut for length - stress is captured in skip_reasons); full MNA-SF total (validated only for 65+, needs BMI/calf measure); any reminder-frequency 'dose' (no trial evidence found). Weekly check-ins carry questionnaire {answers, scores, completedAt}; scores use the ids in 'scoring'.

adjustments.notes: Thresholds are the instruments' own (SNAQ <=14) or their response options; 'two in a row' is a practical rule to avoid over-alerting.

adjustments.when: skip_frequency is '4-7' or '8+', OR snaq_4 is a/b/c (two meals a day or fewer)
adjustments.effect: Phase 1 weekly steps target regular eating before food quality: plan 3 meals plus 1-2 snacks at set times anchored to wake_time and sleep_time, and add one eating occasion per week until the pattern holds. App reminders deliver the planned times.

sources.title: St-Onge MP et al. Meal Timing and Frequency: Implications for Cardiovascular Disease Prevention. AHA Scientific Statement. Circulation 135(9):e96-e121

adjustments.notes: AHA statement: irregular eating patterns appear less favorable for cardiometabolic health; evidence is largely observational. No trial evidence on the best reminder cadence was found, so reminders are only a delivery tool for the planned times, not an evidence-based dose.

adjustments.when: aebq_satiety_responsiveness >= 4 OR snaq_2 is a or b (full after a few mouthfuls or a third of a meal) OR skip_reasons includes 'no_appetite'
adjustments.effect: Smaller, more frequent meals and make each bite count with energy-dense Mediterranean foods: olive oil drizzled on meals, nuts and nut butters, hummus, cheese, yogurt, dried fruit, avocado. Serve snacks between meals rather than right before them (see aebq_sr_3).

disclaimer: This questionnaire helps tailor your meal plan; it isn't a medical test. If your appetite stays low for more than a few weeks, or you're losing weight without trying, please talk with your doctor. Those can have causes worth checking, and they can help you sort it out.
